Sol'Kesh, a sanctuary for life upon a ceaseless horizon spanning ocean, inhabited by plants and animals that have had to evolve and 
struggle to survive isolated for millions of years. Countless species contend for a niche of their own, whether that be the relative 
safety of burrowing beneath the soil, outpacing any predator that stalks the grass-strewn prairies, or growing tall and rising above the 
canopy to unfurl broad emerald leaves and soak in the nourishing rays of the sun. Th ere is a primal balance on this island, a pristine 
environment with fi ve distinct biomes hosting unique flora and fauna to discover. How they respond to the Players (Travelers) that step 
on these untouched lands depends greatly on how the Travelers treat them in kind.
Similar to our own distant history, when mankind fi rst stepped across the Bering Strait into an unseen and untouched new world, 
these ancient explorers walked amongst towering megafauna that would not have known what to make of the sharpened stick wielding 
fur-clad bipeds. Sol'Kesh offers the same primal exploration, replete with beasts that will respond to these intruders with curiosity, 
fear, and hunger. With new horizons to tread, new discoveries to be made, Sol'Kesh unveils a land to explore, to claim, to hunt.
In this bestiary, a Game Master (Keeper) will fi nd everything they need to help guide their storytelling within this natural setting. With 
a wide selection of creatures, locations, and quests, a Keeper can bring this primitive land to life unlike any other. For a Keeper, there's 
a multitude of ways to use the bestiary in their own games, from basing this isolated setting for their world building, adding it as new 
land to be explored in one of their own or existing fantasy worlds, or simply plucking choice creatures from the pages to populate their 
own stories. 
For Travelers, while it may add to the mystery to experience these creatures for the fi rst time, just the same way the beasts will experience 
the strangers within their lands, there is much to be found within these pages to enhance their experience. For a Traveler need not only 
slay the beasts within these pages, for there is the means to tame and befriend, craft and cook, and offers unique feats to aid them in 
navigating this wild land.
Th e Sol’Kesh Speculative Evolution Bestiary is 5e compatible, meaning it plays seamlessly with Dungeons & Dragons, 5th Edition and 
would require the Dungeons and Dragons Core Rulebooks to be played correctly. While most of the rules within this book align with 5e, 
there are some unique features to Sol’Kesh that are highlighted below. Th ese additional features add flavor to the setting and creatures 
of Sol’Kesh, and their use is not mandatory in anyway.
Taming 
Creatures in Sol’Kesh are more than just encounters to slay, a 
Traveler that befriends or captures a creature can eventually 
ally with it through persistent Taming. Th is unique feature is 
represented by the Bond or Control stat, requiring certain levels 
to be obtained before they become Tamed and a life long ally of 
the Traveler. Th is unique feature is further explained on Page 251.
Encountering
Th is lore text further expands on the creature’s behavior and 
helps guide the Keeper in methods in which the Travelers may 
encounter the creature in its natural habitat.
Creature Behavior
To further guide Keepers and Solo Travelers on the natural 
demeanor of the beast, each creature has a Behavior Archetype: 
Aggressive, Defensive, Wary. Th is unique feature is explained on 
Page 256 and describes how the creatures would respond and react 
to an encounter with Travelers. Th is ties directly into Instinct.
Instinct represents a creature’s natural reaction when faced 
with danger and desperation. When certain criteria are met, the 
Keeper rolls for the creature to either succeed or fail its Instinct 
Test. If the result is activated, it then must use its Instinct Ability 
before any other Action. Many creatures have unique Instinct 
abilities that are directly related to their Behavior archetype.
Scavenging
Each adult creature found in the Sol’Kesh Bestiary has three 
Scavenging Components, while the rare and legendary Apex 
creatures have six. Not all Scavenged Components require the 
Travelers to slay the creature, and these Components can be sold 
or used in Crafting, Preparing Meals and Hatching Eggs. Each 
component features the type of item that it can be used for, the 
name of the component, its cost and the DC Test required to 
Scavenge it. Th is unique feature is further explained on Page 246.
